key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings become denser and more corrosion-resistant when droplets flatten well and porosity is minimized, while higher humidity reduces friction and wear through tribo-chemical effects.
engineering_relevance: The study links spray-parameter control and ambient humidity to the durability of Fe-based protective coatings, guiding coating design for corrosion- and wear-critical steel components.
method: Detonation spray Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under varied spray parameters
Compare coating microstructure, porosity, corrosion resistance, and tribological performance
Test wear behavior under different humidity conditions with Si3N4 counterbodies
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that disk-like droplets with higher circularity/expansion form finer, denser lamellar coatings, and that coatings with more porosity show poorer long-term corrosion resistance while friction and wear decrease as humidity increases.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on spray quality and environmental humidity, so results may not directly transfer to other substrates, compositions, or dry-service conditions without re-optimization.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
